finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: The filename 'grades' is hardcoded and not attacker-controlled. However, if this filename were derived from user input, this would be a potential issue.

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.trigger: If 'first' or 'last' contains special characters that are interpreted by the shell (e.g., ';', '|', '&'), this could lead to OS command injection.
finding.assumptions: The 'first' and 'last' fields are populated from user input, and the student struct members 'first' and 'last' are directly used in OS commands without proper sanitization.

finding.title: Improper Resource Management
finding.trigger: If 'strdup' fails to allocate memory, it will return NULL, leading to a null pointer dereference.
finding.assumptions: The 'strdup' function is used to duplicate strings, and it can fail if memory allocation fails. This could lead to a null pointer dereference if the returned pointer is not checked.

finding.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
finding.trigger: If 'exam1', 'exam2', or 'exam3' are very large integers, the sum could overflow, leading to incorrect calculation of the mean.
finding.assumptions: The 'exam1', 'exam2', and 'exam3' fields are populated from user input, and their sum is used to calculate the mean. This could lead to integer overflow if the values are very large.
